BiblicalUsage: Kibshan is a smelting furnace, the place where metal is reduced by fire. Genesis 19:28 shows the smoke of Sodom and Gomorrah going up as the smoke of a furnace, Exodus 19:18 has Sinai itself smoking as a furnace when the LORD descends upon it in fire, and Exodus 9:8 and Exodus 9:10 take handfuls of ashes from the furnace, which Moses sprinkles toward heaven until boils break out on man and beast.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the furnace is God's picture of judgment as refining fire: what goes into it comes out changed, and the smoke of Sodom rises like a warning to every city that forgets Him. I hold that the ashes of the furnace in Egypt became boils on Pharaoh's people, because the fire God lights against the proud always falls on the proud.
